text:
Samir: Quick sync — need a decision on canary end criteria for the routing policy rollout. Two options on the table: sequential monitoring (allow early stop) vs fixed-horizon testing. We also saw a ~3% SRM on the last canary which worries me for early stopping. Thoughts?

Maya: sequential is tempting for speed but increases false positives unless we control alpha spending. suggestion: group-sequential with O'Brien–Fleming style boundaries so early looks are conservative. also enforce a minimum sample size/window. e.g. min N=5k per arm or 30m whichever is larger. :thinking: 

Eli: telemetry gating is critical. regardless of the statistical rule, require latency P50, error rate, and route-assignment skew to be stable for a rolling 10m before any stop/approve. SRM can be a symptom of assignment drift or quota bounces.

Priya: product/pm perspective — console UX needs to show why we stopped early. opaque "early stop due to significance" will freak PMs. we should expose the stopping rule, current alpha spent, SRM, and a link to the raw assignment logs. also a clear rollback button. :thumbsup:

CI Bot: deploy-bot: canary started at 1738642000, variant A=base, B=new-routing, target qps=1200, expected sample/10m ~7k.

Maya: one other thing — if SRM > 1% during the run, pause looks and require ops review. A 3% SRM is big. we should be stricter than before: SRM threshold 1.5% for allowing sequential early stopping, otherwise only fixed-horizon.

Samir: so hybrid: default fixed-horizon, sequential allowed when SRM < X and telemetry gates pass. what should X be? 1.5% sounds ok but is that realistic?

Eli: 1.5% is fine if we also check assignment rate variance and quota hits. Implementation note: we can compute SRM from assigned_count/expected_count per stratum; if stratum-level SRM > threshold, auto-pause canary and open an incidents thread.

Maya: agreed. also pick an overall alpha and spending function. propose two-sided alpha=0.05 with O'Brien–Fleming; operationally we implement a one-sided alpha=0.025 for safety on regressions. early stop only for regression detection, not for superiority unless product signs off.

Priya: product ask — please include in the console: "alpha spent", "look number", "SRM (global + top 3 strata)", "telemetry gates status" and a short explanation link. We should also add an alert if early stop happens so PMs are notified.

Samir: question on numbers: fixed-horizon N — what's reasonable? we expected 7k/10m earlier. want to avoid 30m waits for small effects. propose default fixed-horizon total N=10k per arm or 20k total, with optional override for large customers.

Maya: 10k/arm should detect medium effects (Cohen d ~0.2 with decent power) for latency deltas of ~5-10ms depending on variance. for errors (rare events) need much larger N. we should gate by metric type — e.g., for error rate we always use longer horizon or a separate rare-event detector.

Eli: also add a heuristics check: if p-value dips then spikes (flapping) within 2 looks => treat as non-conclusive and require full horizon. Flapping usually correlates with assignment jitter.

Priya: can we make the console show a "confidence band" and indicate if early-stop was due to p-value or Bayes factor? Some PMs prefer Bayesian interpretability.

Maya: we discussed Bayesian offline but for rollout automation keep frequentist sequential tests — easier to certify and explain. we can add an opt-in Bayesian mode for experimentation teams later.

Samir: concrete decision proposal (so eng/platform can implement):
- Default: fixed-horizon N=10k per arm (or 30m min).
- Allow early stop (sequential monitoring) only if: SRM < 1.5% (global) AND telemetry gates (latency P50, error rate, assignment stability, quota hits) are green for last 10m.
- Statistical rule: one-sided alpha=0.025 for regression detection using O'Brien–Fleming alpha-spending. early stop only for regression.
- For error-rate metrics or low-traffic customers, require separate fixed larger horizon (product will mark metric as "rare-event").
- Console additions: alpha spent, look count, SRM (global + top 3 strata), telemetry gates status, link to raw assignment logs, explicit reason for stop.

Eli: implementation nit — we should compute SRM per stratum and surface the max and a simple histogram. also emit a telemetry event when SRM crosses 0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5% so we can monitor trends.

Priya: +1 to the console fields. Also request a human-in-the-loop checkbox for enterprise rollouts (no auto-approve early stop unless ops confirmed).

Maya: I'll draft the alpha spending params and simulation results for 1.5% SRM threshold and post in the thread. we should simulate with assignment noise.

Samir: ok — final call: implement hybrid described above, ops and product will get console fields + opt-in Bayesian later. I'll file a small RFC and assign implementation to eng-platform. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark: 

CI Bot: deploy-bot: canary partial stop triggered at 1738643000 due to SRM=2.9% (global) — auto-paused. open incident: #INC-4821

Eli: seeing that now — good that pause exists. we'll triage assignment logs and quota metrics.

Priya: noted, PMs notified. will wait for triage before any further action.

Samir: thanks. action items: Maya -> sims + params; Eli -> SRM instrumentation & auto-pause; Priya -> console fields + notifications; I'll write the RFC.
